forecast.<div><br></div><div>As where Tree based models can easily be called with .predict(),</div><div>for LSTM a new sequence must be created (the sequence settings also embedded in forecast object) or as garch model creates forecast based on the length given, it calculates the index difference between feature_date and last calculated residuals time to find out how many iterations are neccesary to provide the forecast for given date</div><div><br></div><div><b>predict_variance_date_single&nbsp;</b>is where those strategies are implemeted. for wide data, basically it is directly with portfolios features for date t. for long format data it is called for every ticker and:</div><div><br></div><div><b>for long format data:</b></div><div>it calculates the prediction for every ticker, then calculates an EWMA covariance matrix with data up to t/ pre variance calculation period. div.div:
Given the MLFeatureResult dataset,
and desired models name with model_name
it creates period_of_forecast forecasts.
thereby takes as last possible feature date as last day in df- period_of_forecast
and trains the model with the data specified in window size
thereby
Last feature date: last day of df -period of forecast
first feature date: last day of df - period of forecast - window size
CREATES ONLY A SINGLE MODEL TRAINED WITH THE WINDOW SIZE
calls rolling_var_forecasting_from_pretrained_model for creating the predictions

div.font: 1) Creates a "residual bank" in form of residual dataframe and initializes it with models initial standart_residuals output. (till day t+1)
(if window size is given, just the latest "window_size" values are taken)
2) Creates a mu_hat / mean realized returns object and initializes it with actual_returns mean in residual bank.

span.font: target date = starts from first date in forecast dates, (t+2 to t+5)
feature date = one day before the forecast date, (t+1 to t+4)

div.font: 1) call predcit_variance_for_date to use model.predict() function
inline with every models internal, and get forecast for target date
2) calculate VaR without updating the residuals or mean realized returns (LOOKAHEAD BIAS PREVENTION) FOR TARGET DATE
3) get realised return for target_date, CALCULATE RESIDUALS FOR TARGET DATE, without updating mu_hat

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 358px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1550px; margin-left: 455px;

div.div:
This function uses the pretrained model given in ForecastResult object and creates additional VaR forecasts, for dates
stated in forecast_dates object. (T+2, T+3, T+4, T+5...)
MLFeatureResult contains NEW features (only return is important) for the forecasting period.
With window_size arrangements, whether to have an expanding or sliding amount of residuals to consider can be managed.
window size > new days to be forecasted will ensure a expanding memory

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 358px; height: 1px; padding-top: 2350px; margin-left: 455px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Used inside the rolling_var_forecasting_from_pretrained_model, this model applies strategies based on the model name in forecast object to calculate a new iteration of model forecast.
As where Tree based models can easily be called with .predict(),
for LSTM a new sequence must be created (the sequence settings also embedded in forecast object) or as garch model creates forecast based on the length given, it calculates the index difference between feature_date and last calculated residuals time to find out how many iterations are neccesary to provide the forecast for given date
predict_variance_date_single is where those strategies are implemeted. for wide data, basically it is directly with portfolios features for date t. for long format data it is called for every ticker and:
for long format data:
it calculates the prediction for every ticker, then calculates an EWMA covariance matrix with data up to t/ pre variance calculation period. Correlation entries in matrix are changed with the models predictions (where correlations are kept) and quadratic form of matrix taken (weighted with portfolio weights) as models prediction for variance.

div.div:
GroundTruthCalendar (data_management.py)
state: train_data, forecast_data, forecast_dates, DANGEROUS_merged_warmedup_FORECAST_data (train+forecast concat, only for boundary warmup lookups), weights, tickers, var_prediction_runs
methods:
- next_bars(dates): position-based next bar over the merged calendar (crosses train/forecast boundary)
- usable_train_dates(candidate_dates, min_periods): intersects caller's candidate_dates with train_data past burn-in, prints the comparison
- forecast_pairs(): (feature_dates, outcome_dates) = (forecast_dates[:-1], forecast_dates[1:])
- add_predicted_var_batch / backtest

div.div: next_bars / usable_train_dates / forecast_pairs moved OUT of tree_models.py's ad-hoc _next_bars() + inline date slicing that used to be duplicated in 3 places.
Calendar now owns next-bar lookup and train/forecast index pairing; callers only supply feature-specific constraints (like common_dates) that the calendar can't know on its own.

div.div:
long_format_train_seed(pooled_model, calendar, training_feature, window_size, ewma_lam, ewma_min_periods) -> (ResidualBank, EwmaVarianceBank) [tree_models.py]
1) common_dates = training_feature.id_cols['Date'].unique()
2) usable_dates = calendar.usable_train_dates(common_dates, ewma_min_periods)
3) outcome_dates = calendar.next_bars(usable_dates)
4) own-day rule: re-key sigma_diag_df from usable_dates -> outcome_dates before EwmaVarianceBank.general_bulk_insert
5) seeds ResidualBank at outcome_dates
6) pending seed for X_out_sample_last_index: calendar.next_bars([train_end]) crosses into forecast via DANGEROUS_merged_warmedup_FORECAST_data to fetch the first forecast bar's actual return — backfills the one bank entry multi_day_var_from_long_format_model can never score itself

predict_variance_batch_long: splits long X via id_cols.groupby('ticker'), scores each ticker through predict_variance_batch_wide
tree_train -> _tree_train_long / _tree_train_wide -> xgboost_train / random_forest_train

div.div:
ResidualBank [data_management.py]
residuals: DataFrame[actual_return, predicted_variance, predicted_sigma, mu_hat, standardized_residual]
own-day rule: Date=X holds the actual_return realized ON X + the predicted_variance produced from X's own PRECEDING feature bar.
step_1_add_residual_with_prev_stateful_mu / step_2_change_stateful_mu — stateful mu_hat, never uses the bar it's currently pricing
training_safe_bulk_insert — sequential bootstrap for the first window_size bars from empty, then hands off to...
general_bulk_insert — vectorized rolling mu_hat (no-look-ahead: window strictly BEFORE t)
windowed_read / empirical_var_for_target / multi_day_var

div.div:
EwmaVarianceBank [data_management.py]
diagonal = per-ticker variance from the ML model; off-diagonal = RiskMetrics-style EWMA correlation on raw ticker returns. Portfolio variance = w^T Sigma_hat w (full quadratic form)
training_safe_bulk_insert — TRAIN-ONLY burn-in (>= ewma_min_periods bars), no output yet
add(date, ticker_return_row, sigma_diag_row) — rolls EWMA forward using the PREVIOUS call's return (self._prev_return), never the return being recorded in the same call
general_bulk_insert — same recursion, vectorized over numpy, one pandas write at the end
cov_by_date, to_dataframe() (returns / sigma_diag / portfolio_variance; cov excluded)

div.div: EwmaVarianceBank.general_bulk_insert in the training seed MUST be called with dates=outcome_dates, not usable_dates/feature_dates.

The EWMA recursion steps using prev_return = R[i-1]. If fed feature dates directly, covs[i] ends up dated for usable_dates[i] while sigma_diag[i] (the ML model's diagonal) is a forecast FOR outcome_dates[i] = usable_dates[i] + 1 bar — a one-bar correlation/diagonal mismatch, and train_end's own return silently never entered the recursion before pricing the first forecast bar.

div.div:
multi_day_var_from_pretrained_model(trained_model, forecast_feature, calendar, window_size, var_confidence, run_key) [data_management.py]
wide/single-ticker path. feature_dates, outcome_dates = calendar.forecast_pairs()
predict -> bank.general_bulk_insert -> bank.multi_day_var -> var_df[varForecast, loss] -> calendar.add_predicted_var_batch
forecast_dates[0] is NEVER scored here — its feature bar is the last TRAINING bar, backfilled instead by long_format_train_seed's pending block

feature_dates, outcome_dates = calendar.forecast_pairs()
predict_variance_batch_long -> sigma_diag_df (indexed by outcome_dates, own-day rule)

bank.general_bulk_insert -> bank.multi_day_var -> var_df -> calendar.add_predicted_var_batch
